scenes.title: 序幕 / 欢迎来到屠宰场
scenes.summary: PC抵达荒凉炎热的阿巴托尔，道路、广播与镇牌营造红色公路开场氛围；这是实际游玩的开端。
scenes.gm_notes: 本场景是实际游玩的开场：1975年7月的西德克萨斯酷热难耐，PC在公路上油量降到半箱以下，看到埃索广告牌与通往阿巴托尔的土路。收音机中郊狼麦克播报高温天气并播放音乐，随后PC抵达破败、近似鬼镇的阿巴托尔。镇中心可见埃索加油站、马瑟综合商店和最后一站食宿酒吧，远处有教堂尖顶；加油站前的几个男人从PC进镇起便盯着他们。页面下半部开始接入“德克萨斯州阿巴托尔镇”的地点说明，并展开“1. 埃索加油站”的描述。
scenes.read_aloud:
西德克萨斯，1975年7月

漫无止境的沥青带仍在不断向前延伸，奔涌的热浪使人无法目测距离，只得闷头驶向远方那低矮山丘与天穹模糊的边界线。还不到上午11点，气温就已经超过了100华氏度，铁皮的汽车内更是宛如蒸笼一般。你们每个人就差脱得精光了，却还是跟刚从游泳池里爬出来一样浑身湿透。而即使摇下车窗也没好到哪里去，外头像是有台工业鼓风机似的输送着热风。你们还有足够的水来维持需求，但水也是温热的，喝起来如同淡茶。

你们听说下一个路边城镇不是很远，但之前的二十英里路连一个限速标志都没看到。油表刚刚也降到了半箱以下，虽然车内没有人吱声，但你们都开始有点紧张了。继续往前开还是干脆回头？不管选哪个可能下场都一样。

然后，你们看到了它——一个褪色的金属广告牌正在阳光下熠熠生辉。上面画了一个开怀大笑的加油站服务员，他戴着一顶俗气的牛仔帽，上世纪50年代的风格。他头顶有一个卡通式的对话气泡，上面写着：你就快到了，伙计！在他下方有个模糊不堪的埃索石油公司的标志。而几乎是路过之后你们才意识到，广告牌的杆子上还有一个小牌子，上面写着：5英里后右转。

正如广告牌承诺的那样，继续飞驰了五英里后，公路的右侧分出一条岔道，不过没有铺沥青，而是条土路。路口有一个倾斜的木头路标插在地上，上面有两块牌子，上面那块写着：3英里后抵达阿巴托尔，下面那块写着提供汽油和食品。

在离开大路之前的某个时刻，你们听到收音机里传来了郊狼麦克的声音，他低沉的男中音像糖浆一样从扬声器里弥漫出来：

“欢迎来到位于地狱第七层的崭新一天，计表上的水漏油。银柱预计要在魔鬼脊背上升到110度，明天也是如此。就像我爷爷常说的：你不能改变风的方向，但是你可以调整风帆以到达目的地。我不知道你们要去哪里，朋友们，但是我可以帮你们在高速公路上摇滚起来！”

然后，收音机里开始播放起Bachman Turner Overdrive乐队的Roll On Down the Highway。

欢迎来到“屠宰场”

尘土飞扬的道路把你们带过一连串的山丘，绕过不知从哪里冒出来的急转弯，穿过一座陈旧的木桥，最后到达阿巴托尔镇。一个手绘的标牌立在镇口，上头写着欢迎来到阿巴托尔，下面一行是人口850。不过很明显，这个标牌很旧了，没有更新以反映该镇的现状。

看起来阿巴托尔与鬼镇相差无几，里面有许多废弃的建筑，空空如也的地洞，以及看起来已经有几十年历史的报废汽车。一条主干道穿街过巷，与几条次要道路之间形成凌乱的夹角。位于城镇中心的是埃索加油站、马瑟综合商店和最后一站食宿酒吧。你们隐约能够看到一座教堂的尖顶掩藏在小路的尽头。几个男人正坐在加油站前面，从你们进镇的那一刻起，他们的目光就死死盯在你们身上。

scene_facts.text: 时间是1975年7月，地点在西德克萨斯。
还不到上午11点，气温已经超过100华氏度；收音机播报最高可能到110度，明天也一样。
PC的车正在公路上行驶，车内酷热难耐，车窗外也是热风。
PC还有足够维持需求的水，但水是温热的。
油表刚刚降到半箱以下。
此前二十英里路上连一个限速标志都没看到。
路边出现褪色的埃索石油广告牌，提示“5英里后右转”。
五英里后，公路右侧分出一条未铺沥青的土路。
岔路口倾斜的木头路标写着“3英里后抵达阿巴托尔”，并标明提供汽油和食品。
收音机里郊狼麦克播报高温天气，并播放Bachman Turner Overdrive的《Roll On Down the Highway》。
土路通往阿巴托尔，途中经过山丘、急转弯和一座陈旧木桥。
镇口手绘标牌写着“欢迎来到阿巴托尔”，人口850，但标牌很旧，显然没有反映现状。
阿巴托尔看起来近似鬼镇，有许多废弃建筑、空洞地洞和几十年历史的报废汽车。
镇内主干道穿过城镇，并与几条次要道路形成凌乱夹角。
镇中心可见埃索加油站、马瑟综合商店和最后一站食宿酒吧。
远处隐约可见一座教堂尖顶，掩藏在小路尽头。
几个男人坐在加油站前，从PC进镇那一刻起就死死盯着他们。

director_facilitation.open_question: PC在燃油下降、酷热和补给压力下，是否进入阿巴托尔并如何接触这个近似鬼镇的镇中心？

pressure_items.text: 酷热难耐：上午不到11点已超过100华氏度，广播称最高预计到110度且明天仍如此。
pressure_items.consequence_hint: 持续高温会加重旅途压力。

pressure_items.text: 油表降到半箱以下，且此前二十英里几乎没有道路设施迹象。
pressure_items.consequence_hint: 继续前进或回头都可能面临燃油与补给压力。

affordance_items.description: 决定在看到阿巴托尔岔路时继续前往、继续沿大路行驶或回头。
查看或利用埃索广告牌与路标提供的方向、汽油和食品信息。
进入镇中心可见的埃索加油站。
前往最后一站食宿酒吧。
沿小路接近远处隐约可见的教堂尖顶。
观察或接触加油站前盯着PC的几个男人。

module_specific_rules.name: 狩猎追逐规则
module_specific_rules.summary: 车辆狩猎使用速度检定、比较速度、敏捷行动顺序、行动点、险境/撞车等流程。

module_specific_rules.name: 开车肇事与撞车结果
module_specific_rules.summary: 车辆撞毁按驾驶检定成功等级决定伤害、报废、翻滚、起火和昏迷等结果；撞人/撞车另有伤害处理。

module_specific_rules.name: 鱼叉弓
module_specific_rules.summary: 沙漠地痞车辆武器，射击（弓术），伤害1D10+2，带牵引绳。

module_specific_rules.name: 豆袋枪
module_specific_rules.summary: 非致命霰弹枪；命中后困难体质检定失败会被击晕2D10分钟。

module_specific_rules.name: 套马杆
module_specific_rules.summary: 以战技将绳圈套住目标肢体或脖颈，多人同时使用可获奖励骰。

module_specific_rules.name: 伊格之眼监视
module_specific_rules.summary: 佩戴者可远程监控六英里以内已知人物或地点，持续12分钟并消耗魔法值。

module_specific_rules.name: 辐射/放射性水环境危害
module_specific_rules.summary: 维兰德矿井部分区域被放射性水淹没，参照附录环境危害。

value.title: 血色公路

setting.tone: 70年代磨坊电影、剥削电影、血浆片风格；粗粝、炎热、孤立、暴力、生存恐怖
setting.place: 西德克萨斯州偏僻公路、阿巴托尔镇及周边沙漠

value.high_concept: 调查员在西德克萨斯偏僻公路上驶入一个几乎被遗忘的小镇阿巴托尔，起初只是为了加油、休息或调查线索，却很快被当地暴力团伙盯上，卷入一场围绕古老蛇神崇拜、沙漠追猎、绑架献祭和逃出生天的生存噩梦。
value.campaign_frame: 本模组适合多种角色类型：倒霉旅行者、政府或环保调查员、失踪人口调查员、神话调查员、电视记者、轰趴青少年等。唯一硬性前提是调查员有理由在1975年夏末开车经过西德克萨斯，并且队伍中至少一人拥有车辆且驾驶技能较高。

warnings: 沙漠高温、脱水与求生压力
safety_recommendations: 开跑前明确告知玩家本模组为成人向、粗粝血浆与生存恐怖风格。
建议使用安全词、X卡、暂停手势或匿名雷区收集。
若玩家要求跳过内容，应立即转场、淡出或改写，不追问原因。
不应让NPC对玩家角色实施强奸；即使剧情逻辑可能导向此处，也应由守密人改写或机械降神避免。
若跳过酷刑或侵犯威胁场景，不应因此额外惩罚玩家角色，例如不应无故追加严重伤害或理智损失。

expected_play_style: 玩家初期以公路旅行或调查为切入点。
第一阶段重点是建立炎热、偏僻、敌意潜伏的小镇氛围。
中期很可能转为汽车追逐、逃亡、求助、躲藏或反击。
后续可走沙盒路线：回镇求助、深入沙漠、调查矿区、寻找失踪者、营救受害者、摧毁邪教据点或单纯逃离。

main_threats: 一群近亲繁衍、暴力而邪教化的沙漠地痞会将外来者视为猎物和祭品。
小镇阿巴托尔并非普通衰败小镇，镇民受到背后邪教与恐惧网络影响。
幕后存在蛇人女祭司艾尔伊希娅·斯丽西·阿娜，她控制泰希罕与沙漠地痞，试图重建伊格神庙并壮大其仆从力量。
疯狂教士、蛇女祭司及其嗜血仆人构成模组主要反派结构。
keeper_only_overview.central_secret: 阿巴托尔及周边区域的失踪、暴力、献祭和怪异活动，最终都与伊格崇拜、蛇人女祭司和其仆从网络有关。
keeper_only_overview.important_mythos_object: 《蠕虫的秘密》是幕后女祭司急于寻回的神话书籍。若有人持有或触碰该书，女祭司能感知其大致位置，除非该人位于特定受保护地点。此内容第一场不应主动暴露，除非调查员选择相关导入并立刻接触该线索。

cold_located_later_chapters: 附录NPC、怪物、狩猎、环境、预设卡

clue_list.clue: 阿巴托尔不在地图上或地图标注异常。
clue_list.delivery: 导航、查看纸质地图、询问本地人。
clue_list.interpretation: 这个地方与正常世界脱节。

clue_list.clue: 镇民对外来者的关注远超正常小镇好奇。
当地人对矿井、水质、失踪者或魔鬼脊背话题明显回避。
有人可能暗示‘天黑前离开’或‘不要走南边/不要停在路上’。
clue_list.delivery: 害怕的普通镇民低声提醒。
clue_list.interpretation: 小镇内有人知道危险，但不敢明说。

clue_list.clue: 车牌、车辆状况或队伍人数被人记录。
clue_list.delivery: 侦查发现，或离开时回想。
clue_list.interpretation: 危险不是随机的，调查员已成为目标。

pacing_plan.beat: 安全工具确认、角色导入、车辆与路线设定。
沙漠公路强开场，缺油或过热压力，发现阿巴托尔路牌。
抵达加油站和镇入口，第一次NPC互动，建立不适感。
自由探索一到两个镇内地点，获取补给与少量线索。
威胁升级：被盯梢、车辆被检查、收到警告或发生轻微挑衅。
以调查员决定离开、留下过夜、继续调查或被尾随作为悬念收尾。

clues.clue: 阿巴托尔路牌宣称前方有50英里内唯一加油站。
纸质地图上找不到阿巴托尔，或位置与路牌不符。
clues.meaning: 暗示小镇异常、偏僻或被遗忘。
clues.delivery: 导航或图书馆使用/相关知识可发现；也可由细心玩家看地图自动发现。

first_scenes.title: 热浪中的公路
first_scenes.purpose: 建立环境压力、时代感和孤立感；让玩家定义人物关系和车辆状态。

possible_checks.use: 处理崎岖路段、爆胎前兆、引擎过热或避开路面障碍。失败可造成时间损失、车辆轻微损耗或增加紧张感。
确认地图与路牌不一致，发现阿巴托尔似乎不在常规公路地图上。
从广播噪音中听到郊狼麦克提到天气、魔鬼脊背或某种不祥玩笑。
判断车辆还能撑多久，或暂时处理过热问题。

sensory_details: 空气像从烤箱里吹出来。
收音机只有乡村摇滚、布道节目和郊狼麦克的杂音。
远处偶尔有废弃棚屋和生锈风车。

clues.clue: 镇民对外来者的车、人数和目的异常关注。
clues.meaning: 调查员已经被标记为外来者。
clues.delivery: 侦查或心理学；也可通过对话感受。

clues.clue: 有人建议他们去镇上的酒吧或餐厅休息，口气像是在把他们引向固定路线。
clues.meaning: 本地人可能在观察或配合某种流程。

clues.clue: 电话线路、地图、警局或公路信息都不可靠。
clues.meaning: 外援和正常文明秩序在这里失效。

first_scenes.title: 欢迎来到阿巴托尔
first_scenes.purpose: 让调查员进入小镇，获得第一印象：荒废、炎热、敌意隐藏在日常背后。
first_scenes.location: 阿巴托尔镇入口与埃索加油站周边

possible_checks.use: 注意到有人从窗后观察，或某辆车似乎在远处停了很久。
判断镇民的友善并不自然，像是恐惧、敌意或排练好的冷漠。
以身份、职业或金钱争取服务，例如加油、问路或使用电话。
让镇民透露有限信息。
短期压服某个普通镇民，但可能让敌意升级。

first_impressions: 小镇不像完全废弃，却没有正常生活的活力。
镇民可能冷淡、盯视、过度礼貌或故意回避。
炎热和尘土让所有事情都显得迟缓而压抑。
first_scenes.read_aloud_style_prompt: 阿巴托尔比你们想象中更安静。几栋低矮建筑趴在太阳底下，招牌掉漆，窗帘半掩，街上看不到几个行人。加油站的埃索标志褪成了旧血一样的红色。远处某处有狗叫，又很快停了。你们的车驶进镇里时，几扇窗后的影子似乎动了一下。

beats: 调查员购买燃料、水、食物或修车用品。
一个或多个本地人用过于直白的目光打量他们。
若调查员询问失踪人口、矿井、镇史或奇怪传闻，镇民会变得紧张或敷衍。
若调查员炫耀现金、装备、摄像机或孤立无援，会更快吸引猎手注意。
离开前，给出一处不祥细节：车上出现陌生手印、有人记下车牌、远处有发动机声、或一辆本地车慢慢跟出镇外。
first_scenes.title: 燃料、热饭与坏目光
first_scenes.purpose: 给玩家短暂补给机会，同时让威胁开始靠近。
first_scenes.location: 埃索加油站、镇中心、酒吧或餐厅

possible_checks.use: 发现有人在观察车辆、检查车牌或靠近后备箱。
听到本地人低声说‘外地人’、‘今晚’、‘路上’等片段。
检查车辆是否被动手脚；第一场可只给轻微问题或疑似痕迹，不必立即摊牌。
意识到某些NPC并非单纯排外，而是在害怕某个更大的东西。

escalation_options: 温和版：调查员只是被盯上，离镇时有车远远尾随。
标准版：本地人试图拖延他们，例如说油泵慢、电话坏、路况危险。
强硬版：若调查员挑衅或调查过深，有人试图破坏车辆、偷走水或引诱他们走错路。

immediate_pressure: 车辆燃油不足或引擎过热。
天气炎热，水和阴影都显得宝贵。
手机不存在或无信号时代背景下，外援极其有限。
地图上可能没有阿巴托尔，或标注模糊不一致。
strong_start.read_aloud_style_prompt: 西德克萨斯的公路在热浪里发抖。车窗外是一望无际的尘土、毛线稷、歪斜电线杆和被太阳晒褪色的广告牌。收音机时断时续，一个自称“郊狼麦克”的DJ在杂音里开着不合时宜的玩笑。油表已经低得让人不安。就在你们开始怀疑下一座城镇是否真实存在时，一块旧路牌从热雾中浮现：前方加油站，50英里内唯一燃料。箭头指向：阿巴托尔。
opening_question_for_players: 你们为什么会在1975年夏末开车经过这段西德克萨斯公路？
谁在开车？这辆车是什么型号、状况如何？
车里现在最紧张的事情是什么：缺油、迷路、争吵、任务压力，还是某个失踪者线索？

value.session_scope: 第一场至第一晚：调查员驶入阿巴托尔，感受小镇异常，获得燃料或食物，初步接触镇民，并被潜在猎手注意。不要提前展开后续基地、矿井、蛇洞章节；只冷定位这些地点。

required_player_setup.driver: 至少一名调查员驾驶技能建议55%以上。
era_reminders: 导航依靠纸质地图、路牌、加油站问路和广播。
车载电话极其罕见，不应默认存在。
现金、汽油、水、备胎、工具和武器会变得重要。
suggested_vehicles: 电视台采访车或厢式货车

conflicts_and_pressures.conflict: 补给需求 vs. 敌意环境
conflicts_and_pressures.description: 调查员需要燃料、水、食物、电话或修车，但每次停留都会让更多人注意他们。

conflicts_and_pressures.conflict: 正常解释 vs. 恐怖直觉
conflicts_and_pressures.description: 一切都可以暂时解释为贫穷、排外、沙漠孤立和小镇衰败，但细节逐渐不对劲。
若调查员只是想走，后续追猎可自然开启；若他们主动调查，小镇秘密会更早被触碰。

conflicts_and_pressures.conflict: 公开身份 vs. 低调行动
conflicts_and_pressures.description: 记者、政府人员或侦探身份能打开一些门，也会让敌人更快警觉。

recommended_character_hooks.use: 最直接。调查员只是走了最短路线，结果被迫在阿巴托尔停车。
调查员来检测废弃铀矿附近地下水或环境污染。第一场可以让他们特别关注水厂、矿区传闻和镇民回避态度。
调查员追查某个最后在“魔鬼脊背”一带出现的人。阿巴托尔是自然问询点。
调查员来拍摄关于铀矿开采影响的专题。摄影机、录音设备和采访会激怒或吸引镇民。
调查员因古老文件提到蛇人遗迹而来。第一场应只给轻微暗示，不要过早揭示幕后真相。
调查员来沙漠狂欢、兜风或逃离家庭压力。适合强化血浆片和公路恐怖感。

keeper_only_do_not_reveal_yet: 不要在第一场直接揭示蛇人女祭司的身份与计划。
不要完整解释泰希罕、基地、蛇洞或伊格神庙。
不要提前展开后续章节地图。
除非玩家主动走向相关地点，否则不要把矿井、基地或蛇洞作为第一场实景。

key_locations_for_first_session.name: 西德克萨斯偏僻公路
key_locations_for_first_session.use_now: 开场公路、热浪、缺油、孤立、导入角色关系。
key_locations_for_first_session.keeper_notes: 强调前后几十英里无人烟，让玩家理解车辆就是生命线。

key_locations_for_first_session.name: 阿巴托尔镇
key_locations_for_first_session.use_now: 第一幕主要沙盒区域。玩家可在镇中找燃料、食物、电话、问路或调查。
key_locations_for_first_session.keeper_notes: 保持镇民表现为压抑、冷漠、窥视、恐惧或奇怪热情。不要过早说明他们与幕后邪教的关系。

key_locations_for_first_session.name: 埃索加油站
key_locations_for_first_session.use_now: 最自然的第一停靠点，提供汽油、问路、第一批NPC互动。
key_locations_for_first_session.keeper_notes: 这是让调查员以为仍在普通世界中的最后机会。

key_locations_for_first_session.name: 酒吧/餐厅
key_locations_for_first_session.use_now: 让调查员吃饭、休息、听流言、感受敌意。
key_locations_for_first_session.keeper_notes: 可以放置自动点唱机、郊狼麦克广播、沉默镇民和观察者。

key_locations_for_first_session.name: 镇中心若干商铺
key_locations_for_first_session.use_now: 若玩家主动探索，可即兴提供基本服务，如杂货、药店、五金、理发店等。
key_locations_for_first_session.keeper_notes: 不要全面展开目录中所有地点；只准备一两个玩家主动进入的地点。

key_locations_for_first_session.name: 基地、老矿场、维兰德矿井、蛇洞
key_locations_for_first_session.use_now: 第一场不主动开放细节。
key_locations_for_first_session.keeper_notes: 可作为流言、路牌、失踪线索或镇民回避的话题存在。

important_npcs_for_first_session.name: 郊狼麦克
important_npcs_for_first_session.public_face: 播放1970年代音乐、天气、路况和随口玩笑。
important_npcs_for_first_session.use_at_table: 用他来加强时代氛围，也可让他的评论与当前事件形成不祥巧合。
important_npcs_for_first_session.keeper_secret: 目前只作为氛围工具即可，不必赋予实质剧情功能。

important_npcs_for_first_session.name: 埃索加油站工作人员
important_npcs_for_first_session.motives: 避免惹麻烦；观察外来者；可能暗中向更危险的人传递消息。
important_npcs_for_first_session.appears_as: 疲惫、晒伤、寡言或过度热情的本地人
important_npcs_for_first_session.public_face: 愿意卖油，但对路线、警察、电话、失踪人口等问题含糊其辞。
important_npcs_for_first_session.keeper_secret: 是否直接配合沙漠地痞可按节奏决定。第一场重点是制造不适，而非直接暴露。

important_npcs_for_first_session.name: 沉默的本地顾客
important_npcs_for_first_session.motives: 评估调查员人数、武器、车辆、是否容易下手。
important_npcs_for_first_session.appears_as: 坐在角落、卡车旁或酒吧里的本地男人/女人
important_npcs_for_first_session.public_face: 盯着调查员，不主动开口，或只说短句。
important_npcs_for_first_session.keeper_secret: 可作为沙漠地痞的眼线或同情者。

important_npcs_for_first_session.name: 害怕的普通镇民
important_npcs_for_first_session.appears_as: 店员、老人、洗衣店顾客、杂货店雇员或路边孩子的家长
important_npcs_for_first_session.public_face: 不敢多说，但可能用眼神、纸条或含糊警告暗示调查员快走。
important_npcs_for_first_session.keeper_secret: 适合在玩家善待NPC、低调询问或表现出同理心时出现。

important_npcs_for_first_session.name: 沙漠地痞观察者
important_npcs_for_first_session.motives: 标记猎物，判断何时在镇外动手。
important_npcs_for_first_session.appears_as: 皮卡里的粗野本地人、修车棚旁的男人、酒吧外抽烟的人
important_npcs_for_first_session.public_face: 粗鲁调笑、盯视、打量车辆，可能挑衅。
important_npcs_for_first_session.keeper_secret: 他们计划在调查员离镇后展开追踪或伏击；第一场可让他们只出现为远处威胁。

possible_session_end_cliffhangers: 调查员驶离阿巴托尔，后视镜里出现一辆没有开灯的皮卡。
他们回到车边，发现油箱盖被打开，车身上有尘土手印。
一名害怕的镇民塞给他们一张纸条：别等天黑。
酒吧自动点唱机突然停下，全场安静，所有人都看向调查员。
收音机里的郊狼麦克笑着说：‘今晚魔鬼脊背可不太平，朋友们。’随后信号断成一片白噪音。

module_overview.title: 血色公路

setting.tone: 70年代磨坊电影、剥削电影、血浆片风格；粗粝、炎热、孤立、暴力、生存恐怖
setting.place: 西德克萨斯州偏僻公路、阿巴托尔镇及周边沙漠

module_overview.high_concept: 调查员在西德克萨斯偏僻公路上驶入一个几乎被遗忘的小镇阿巴托尔，起初只是为了加油、休息或调查线索，却很快被当地暴力团伙盯上，卷入一场围绕古老蛇神崇拜、沙漠追猎、绑架献祭和逃出生天的生存噩梦。
module_overview.campaign_frame: 本模组适合多种角色类型：倒霉旅行者、政府或环保调查员、失踪人口调查员、神话调查员、电视记者、轰趴青少年等。唯一硬性前提是调查员有理由在1975年夏末开车经过西德克萨斯，并且队伍中至少一人拥有车辆且驾驶技能较高。

warnings: 沙漠高温、脱水与求生压力
safety_recommendations: 开跑前明确告知玩家本模组为成人向、粗粝血浆与生存恐怖风格。
建议使用安全词、X卡、暂停手势或匿名雷区收集。
若玩家要求跳过内容，应立即转场、淡出或改写，不追问原因。
不应让NPC对玩家角色实施强奸；即使剧情逻辑可能导向此处，也应由守密人改写或机械降神避免。
若跳过酷刑或侵犯威胁场景，不应因此额外惩罚玩家角色，例如不应无故追加严重伤害或理智损失。

expected_play_style: 玩家初期以公路旅行或调查为切入点。
第一阶段重点是建立炎热、偏僻、敌意潜伏的小镇氛围。
中期很可能转为汽车追逐、逃亡、求助、躲藏或反击。
后续可走沙盒路线：回镇求助、深入沙漠、调查矿区、寻找失踪者、营救受害者、摧毁邪教据点或单纯逃离。

main_threats: 一群近亲繁衍、暴力而邪教化的沙漠地痞会将外来者视为猎物和祭品。
小镇阿巴托尔并非普通衰败小镇，镇民受到背后邪教与恐惧网络影响。
幕后存在蛇人女祭司艾尔伊希娅·斯丽西·阿娜，她控制泰希罕与沙漠地痞，试图重建伊格神庙并壮大其仆从力量。
疯狂教士、蛇女祭司及其嗜血仆人构成模组主要反派结构。
keeper_only_overview.central_secret: 阿巴托尔及周边区域的失踪、暴力、献祭和怪异活动，最终都与伊格崇拜、蛇人女祭司和其仆从网络有关。
keeper_only_overview.important_mythos_object: 《蠕虫的秘密》是幕后女祭司急于寻回的神话书籍。若有人持有或触碰该书，女祭司能感知其大致位置，除非该人位于特定受保护地点。此内容第一场不应主动暴露，除非调查员选择相关导入并立刻接触该线索。

cold_located_later_chapters: 附录NPC、怪物、狩猎、环境、预设卡

clue_list.clue: 阿巴托尔不在地图上或地图标注异常。
clue_list.delivery: 导航、查看纸质地图、询问本地人。
clue_list.interpretation: 这个地方与正常世界脱节。

clue_list.clue: 镇民对外来者的关注远超正常小镇好奇。
当地人对矿井、水质、失踪者或魔鬼脊背话题明显回避。
有人可能暗示‘天黑前离开’或‘不要走南边/不要停在路上’。
clue_list.delivery: 害怕的普通镇民低声提醒。
clue_list.interpretation: 小镇内有人知道危险，但不敢明说。

clue_list.clue: 车牌、车辆状况或队伍人数被人记录。
clue_list.delivery: 侦查发现，或离开时回想。
clue_list.interpretation: 危险不是随机的，调查员已成为目标。

pacing_plan.beat: 安全工具确认、角色导入、车辆与路线设定。
沙漠公路强开场，缺油或过热压力，发现阿巴托尔路牌。
抵达加油站和镇入口，第一次NPC互动，建立不适感。
自由探索一到两个镇内地点，获取补给与少量线索。
威胁升级：被盯梢、车辆被检查、收到警告或发生轻微挑衅。
以调查员决定离开、留下过夜、继续调查或被尾随作为悬念收尾。

clues.clue: 阿巴托尔路牌宣称前方有50英里内唯一加油站。
纸质地图上找不到阿巴托尔，或位置与路牌不符。
clues.meaning: 暗示小镇异常、偏僻或被遗忘。
clues.delivery: 导航或图书馆使用/相关知识可发现；也可由细心玩家看地图自动发现。

first_scenes.title: 热浪中的公路
first_scenes.purpose: 建立环境压力、时代感和孤立感；让玩家定义人物关系和车辆状态。

possible_checks.use: 处理崎岖路段、爆胎前兆、引擎过热或避开路面障碍。失败可造成时间损失、车辆轻微损耗或增加紧张感。
确认地图与路牌不一致，发现阿巴托尔似乎不在常规公路地图上。
从广播噪音中听到郊狼麦克提到天气、魔鬼脊背或某种不祥玩笑。
判断车辆还能撑多久，或暂时处理过热问题。

sensory_details: 空气像从烤箱里吹出来。
收音机只有乡村摇滚、布道节目和郊狼麦克的杂音。
远处偶尔有废弃棚屋和生锈风车。

clues.clue: 镇民对外来者的车、人数和目的异常关注。
clues.meaning: 调查员已经被标记为外来者。
clues.delivery: 侦查或心理学；也可通过对话感受。

clues.clue: 有人建议他们去镇上的酒吧或餐厅休息，口气像是在把他们引向固定路线。
clues.meaning: 本地人可能在观察或配合某种流程。

clues.clue: 电话线路、地图、警局或公路信息都不可靠。
clues.meaning: 外援和正常文明秩序在这里失效。

first_scenes.title: 欢迎来到阿巴托尔
first_scenes.purpose: 让调查员进入小镇，获得第一印象：荒废、炎热、敌意隐藏在日常背后。
first_scenes.location: 阿巴托尔镇入口与埃索加油站周边

possible_checks.use: 注意到有人从窗后观察，或某辆车似乎在远处停了很久。
判断镇民的友善并不自然，像是恐惧、敌意或排练好的冷漠。
以身份、职业或金钱争取服务，例如加油、问路或使用电话。
让镇民透露有限信息。
短期压服某个普通镇民，但可能让敌意升级。

first_impressions: 小镇不像完全废弃，却没有正常生活的活力。
镇民可能冷淡、盯视、过度礼貌或故意回避。
炎热和尘土让所有事情都显得迟缓而压抑。
first_scenes.read_aloud_style_prompt: 阿巴托尔比你们想象中更安静。几栋低矮建筑趴在太阳底下，招牌掉漆，窗帘半掩，街上看不到几个行人。加油站的埃索标志褪成了旧血一样的红色。远处某处有狗叫，又很快停了。你们的车驶进镇里时，几扇窗后的影子似乎动了一下。

beats: 调查员购买燃料、水、食物或修车用品。
一个或多个本地人用过于直白的目光打量他们。
若调查员询问失踪人口、矿井、镇史或奇怪传闻，镇民会变得紧张或敷衍。
若调查员炫耀现金、装备、摄像机或孤立无援，会更快吸引猎手注意。
离开前，给出一处不祥细节：车上出现陌生手印、有人记下车牌、远处有发动机声、或一辆本地车慢慢跟出镇外。
first_scenes.title: 燃料、热饭与坏目光
first_scenes.purpose: 给玩家短暂补给机会，同时让威胁开始靠近。
first_scenes.location: 埃索加油站、镇中心、酒吧或餐厅

possible_checks.use: 发现有人在观察车辆、检查车牌或靠近后备箱。
听到本地人低声说‘外地人’、‘今晚’、‘路上’等片段。
检查车辆是否被动手脚；第一场可只给轻微问题或疑似痕迹，不必立即摊牌。
意识到某些NPC并非单纯排外，而是在害怕某个更大的东西。

escalation_options: 温和版：调查员只是被盯上，离镇时有车远远尾随。
标准版：本地人试图拖延他们，例如说油泵慢、电话坏、路况危险。
强硬版：若调查员挑衅或调查过深，有人试图破坏车辆、偷走水或引诱他们走错路。

immediate_pressure: 车辆燃油不足或引擎过热。
天气炎热，水和阴影都显得宝贵。
手机不存在或无信号时代背景下，外援极其有限。
地图上可能没有阿巴托尔，或标注模糊不一致。
strong_start.read_aloud_style_prompt: 西德克萨斯的公路在热浪里发抖。车窗外是一望无际的尘土、毛线稷、歪斜电线杆和被太阳晒褪色的广告牌。收音机时断时续，一个自称“郊狼麦克”的DJ在杂音里开着不合时宜的玩笑。油表已经低得让人不安。就在你们开始怀疑下一座城镇是否真实存在时，一块旧路牌从热雾中浮现：前方加油站，50英里内唯一燃料。箭头指向：阿巴托尔。
opening_question_for_players: 你们为什么会在1975年夏末开车经过这段西德克萨斯公路？
谁在开车？这辆车是什么型号、状况如何？
车里现在最紧张的事情是什么：缺油、迷路、争吵、任务压力，还是某个失踪者线索？

current_session_packet.session_scope: 第一场至第一晚：调查员驶入阿巴托尔，感受小镇异常，获得燃料或食物，初步接触镇民，并被潜在猎手注意。不要提前展开后续基地、矿井、蛇洞章节；只冷定位这些地点。

required_player_setup.driver: 至少一名调查员驾驶技能建议55%以上。
era_reminders: 导航依靠纸质地图、路牌、加油站问路和广播。
车载电话极其罕见，不应默认存在。
现金、汽油、水、备胎、工具和武器会变得重要。
suggested_vehicles: 电视台采访车或厢式货车

conflicts_and_pressures.conflict: 补给需求 vs. 敌意环境
conflicts_and_pressures.description: 调查员需要燃料、水、食物、电话或修车，但每次停留都会让更多人注意他们。

conflicts_and_pressures.conflict: 正常解释 vs. 恐怖直觉
conflicts_and_pressures.description: 一切都可以暂时解释为贫穷、排外、沙漠孤立和小镇衰败，但细节逐渐不对劲。
若调查员只是想走，后续追猎可自然开启；若他们主动调查，小镇秘密会更早被触碰。

conflicts_and_pressures.conflict: 公开身份 vs. 低调行动
conflicts_and_pressures.description: 记者、政府人员或侦探身份能打开一些门，也会让敌人更快警觉。

recommended_character_hooks.use: 最直接。调查员只是走了最短路线，结果被迫在阿巴托尔停车。
调查员来检测废弃铀矿附近地下水或环境污染。第一场可以让他们特别关注水厂、矿区传闻和镇民回避态度。
调查员追查某个最后在“魔鬼脊背”一带出现的人。阿巴托尔是自然问询点。
调查员来拍摄关于铀矿开采影响的专题。摄影机、录音设备和采访会激怒或吸引镇民。

一名害怕的镇民塞给他们一张纸条：别等天黑。
酒吧自动点唱机突然停下，全场安静，所有人都看向调查员。

scenes.title: Introduction
scenes.summary: Mr. Steven Knott hires the investigators to examine the Corbitt House in 1920s Boston after the Macario tragedy made it impossible to rent.
scenes.read_aloud: It is 1920 in Boston. Mr. Steven Knott, a landlord with a problem property, meets you with the keys and a retainer. The old Corbitt House has a violent reputation after the Macario family fled or collapsed into illness and madness. Knott wants the truth found and the house made rentable again. He gives you the address, keys, and $20 in advance, then waits to hear how you intend to begin the investigation.
scenes.gm_notes: Keep Mr. Knott mundane and anxious about money. He can confirm he recently inherited the property, cannot rent or sell it, and expects research before a risky visit. Do not expose the Keeper secret.

links.reason: Newspaper research can reveal the house history.
Library research can reveal Corbitt property history.
Civil records can reveal the executor and chapel link.
Court and police files can reveal the 1912 raid.
Neighbors may remember recent tenants and local rumors.
The surviving Macario family can provide firsthand testimony.
The chapel clue can be physically followed up.
The investigators can visit the house once ready.

scenes.title: The Boston Globe
scenes.summary: The newspaper morgue can reveal the house has a long pattern of violent accidents, illness, suicide, and the Macario case.
scenes.read_aloud: The Boston Globe offices smell of ink, paper dust, and hot machinery. Staff can point you toward the basement clippings morgue, but the files are not open to casual visitors; an editor named Arty Wilmot controls access.
scenes.gm_notes: To access the clippings files, choose Charm/Persuade/Intimidate/Fast Talk according to player approach; Regular difficulty. On success, Ruth Blake takes them to the dusty morgue and Handout 2 becomes obvious by street address. On failure, Arty refuses; pushed failure should escalate beyond simple refusal.

links.reason: Follow up older property references at the library.
Civil records may predate surviving newspaper files.
The investigators can visit the house.

checks.failure: Arty denies access; pushed failure escalates

scenes.title: The Central Library
scenes.summary: Library research can reveal the house was built in 1835, bought by Walter Corbitt, litigated over his behavior, and tied to a contested basement burial.
scenes.read_aloud: The Central Library is quiet, formal, and full of old catalogues. The Corbitt House trail is not in one neat place; it will take careful half-day blocks of research to bring useful records together.
scenes.gm_notes: Each half-day of research asks for Library Use. For each success, reveal handouts 3-6 in order. If research exceeds a day, Mr. Knott checks in and presses for progress.

links.reason: The executor/church trail points toward civil records.
The chapel records may require higher court or police access.
The investigators can visit the house.

scenes.title: Hall of Records
scenes.summary: Civil records reveal Corbitt’s executor was Reverend Michael Thomas of the Chapel of Contemplation; church records note the chapel closure in 1912.
scenes.read_aloud: At the Hall of Records, bound registers and civil files sit behind clerks and indexes. The name Corbitt leads toward an executor, a church, and a closure date that does not feel ordinary.
scenes.gm_notes: Ask for Library Use. On success reveal Handout 7. Courteous clerk or Law can point toward county/commonwealth/federal courts and Central Police Station for serious-crime records.

links.reason: Serious-crime and police records may hold the missing chapel raid file.
The Chapel of Contemplation can be investigated directly.
The investigators can visit the house.

checks.success: reveal executor and Chapel of Contemplation connection

scenes.title: Higher Courts and Central Police Station
scenes.summary: Restricted records reveal a secret 1912 raid on the Chapel of Contemplation, deaths, missing autopsy detail, released cultists, official interference, and Michael Thomas’s conviction and escape.
scenes.read_aloud: Court and police records are less welcoming than public archives. Clerks, officers, and locked files make this a social or professional access problem before it becomes a research problem.
scenes.gm_notes: Access requires Law, Credit Rating 75+, Persuade, Charm, or Fast Talk as justified by roleplay. On success reveal Handout 8. On pushed failure, consequences can include police antipathy, threat, shakedown, or a bribe trap.

links.reason: The police file makes the chapel a concrete lead.
The investigators can visit the house.

scenes.title: The Neighborhood
scenes.summary: Neighbors near the Corbitt House can provide rumors and firsthand color about the house and the Macario family.
scenes.read_aloud: The streets around the Corbitt House carry the ordinary noise of Boston, but doors close a little faster when the address is mentioned. Some residents remember the Macarios; some would rather not talk.
scenes.gm_notes: Roleplay questioning neighbors. Mr. Dooley is a useful local contact. Use social skills only when pressure, credibility, or deception matters; success should produce concrete rumor or firsthand detail.

links.reason: Macario family testimony can be followed at the sanitarium.
The investigators can visit the house.

scenes.title: Roxbury Sanitarium
scenes.summary: The surviving Macario testimony points to something active in the house and may suggest Corbitt can be killed with his own dagger.
scenes.read_aloud: Roxbury Sanitarium is sterile, controlled, and sad. The Macario name opens a narrow path to a damaged witness, but whatever happened in the Corbitt House has not left him whole.
scenes.gm_notes: Vittorio Macario is unstable and frightened. Handle with care. If the investigators build enough trust or read his reactions, reveal that he fears the house and may understand that Corbitt can be killed with his own dagger.

links.reason: The dagger clue points toward the house basement and hidden threat.
The investigators can visit the house.

scenes.title: The Chapel of Contemplation
scenes.summary: The ruined chapel can yield occult records, the symbol handout, and the decisive clue that Walter Corbitt was buried in the basement of his house.
scenes.read_aloud: The Chapel of Contemplation is a ruin with a bad history and newer signs of disturbance. Dust, collapsed masonry, and a few surviving records make the place feel abandoned rather than empty.
scenes.gm_notes: Searching the cabinet can reveal old records. Handout 9 is the symbol. A key record states Corbitt was buried in the basement of his house in accordance with his wishes. Treat that as a concrete clue, not flavor.

links.reason: The burial clue points to the basement.
The investigators can visit the house.

data.obvious_clue: Walter Corbitt was buried in his house basement.

scenes.title: The Old Corbitt Place
scenes.summary: The investigators arrive at the old house; exterior entry and initial inspection set the frame for room exploration.
scenes.read_aloud: The Corbitt House waits behind its old address with the tired look of a place that has been explained away too many times. The keys fit. The windows are still, the air around the threshold stale.
scenes.gm_notes: Let players inspect entrances, windows, neighbors, or go inside. Do not force an option list. Keep hidden basement truth unrevealed until found through play.

links.reason: Entering the house leads to the ground floor.
The surrounding neighborhood can still be canvassed.

scenes.title: Corbitt House: Ground Floor
scenes.summary: Ground-floor rooms establish the derelict house, possible diaries/books, doors, kitchen, storage, and access toward upper floor or basement.
scenes.read_aloud: Inside, the house smells of old plaster, dust, and trapped damp. Everyday rooms have gone stale: furniture under grime, corners gone dark, and the sense that small noises carry too far.
scenes.gm_notes: Adjudicate room-by-room inspection. Searching can produce mundane details and any source-backed papers/books from rooms. Let player movement decide whether they go upstairs or down.

links.reason: Stairs lead up to the bedrooms.
A basement stair/door leads downward.
The exterior remains accessible.

scenes.title: Corbitt House: Upper Floor
scenes.summary: Upper-floor bedrooms include Macario family spaces and the dangerous animated bed event.
scenes.read_aloud: Upstairs, the bedrooms still hold traces of a family interrupted: small beds, religious items, stale bedding, and a silence that makes every floorboard answer back.
scenes.gm_notes: If the bed attack triggers, ask Spot Hidden if appropriate, then Dodge to avoid being hit/thrown; seeing impossible movement requires SAN 0/1 or 1/1D4 as source notes indicate. Keep window positioning clear and impartial.

links.reason: The stairs return to the ground floor.
The investigation can move downward.

hazards.sanity: 1 point or 1D4 depending failure as source notes

scenes.title: Corbitt House: The Basement
scenes.summary: The basement contains a dangerous stair/door, the floating magical dagger, storage spaces, rats, and the concealed path to Corbitt’s lair.
scenes.read_aloud: The basement air is colder and wetter. Rough boards, old bins, and a dark under-space make the room feel less like storage than concealment.
scenes.gm_notes: Resolve dangerous descent with DEX/Climb when warranted. The floating dagger uses Corbitt’s POW and source rules; seeing it attack calls for SAN 1/1D4. Breaking/removing boards reveals crawl space, rats, and the carved Chapel clue; the inner wall can lead to Corbitt’s hiding place.

links.reason: Breaking through the hidden wall reveals Corbitt’s hiding place.
The stairs return upward.

scenes.title: Corbitt’s Hidden Lair
scenes.summary: The hidden room contains Corbitt’s undead body, papers, final confrontation, Sanity loss, combat, possible Dominate, Flesh Ward, and victory/failure outcomes.
scenes.read_aloud: Beyond the broken wall is a fouler space. On a pallet lies a tall, wasted figure, wood-dry and hairless, with a chain at its neck and a sweet rotten smell in the air. Curled papers sit on a small table in the corner.
scenes.gm_notes: When Corbitt rises, call for SAN 1/1D8. He has STR 90, CON 115, SIZ 55, INT 80, POW 90, DEX 35, APP 05, EDU 80, HP 16, MP 18, Fighting 50%, Dodge 17%, Flesh Ward armor 2D6 already cast, Dominate variant, floating dagger. If reduced to 0 HP he crumbles. If stabbed with his own dagger he quickly turns to ash regardless of spells. Victory pays fee plus bonus and grants 1D6 SAN.

links.reason: If Corbitt is destroyed or the investigators withdraw/fail, resolve the ending.

opponent.armor: Flesh Ward 2D6, depletes by damage blocked

scenes.title: Conclusion
scenes.summary: If Corbitt is destroyed, Knott pays promptly and each participating investigator gains 1D6 SAN; failure can leave Knott dead and police suspicion on the investigators.
scenes.gm_notes: Use source ending conditions. Do not declare a win without resolving Corbitt or a credible alternative. If investigators knowingly leave the threat active, report consequences honestly.

dice_core.summary: Core resolution is percentile roll-under. When the Keeper calls for a roll, the player rolls 1d100 against the relevant skill or other rating. A result above the rating fails; a result equal to or below it succeeds. Difficulty can tighten the target by using a fraction of the rating rather than the full value: the pages read explicitly show a Hard success as rolling less than half the investigator’s Drive Auto skill. Sanity uses the same procedure: the Keeper calls for a Sanity roll, and on failure the investigator loses the listed amount for that encounter (example given: 0/1d6).
dice_core.compare_to: the relevant skill or characteristic value; harder difficulties use fractions of that value
dice_core.success_rule: Roll 1d100 and succeed if the result is equal to or less than the relevant rating; if a harder difficulty is called for, succeed only if the roll is equal to or less than the required fraction of that rating (explicitly, half for Hard).

success_bands.label: Hard success
success_bands.semantics: A stronger degree of success, showing notably capable performance. In opposed situations it beats a regular success and loses to an extreme or critical result.

success_bands.label: Regular success
success_bands.semantics: An ordinary success: the investigator achieves the intended task under the current difficulty.

success_bands.label: Failure
success_bands.semantics: The investigator does not achieve the stated goal; the Keeper narrates the failed outcome and may apply the stated consequences or allow a push where appropriate.

success_bands.label: Extreme
success_bands.semantics: A result equal to or below one-fifth of the relevant skill or characteristic. It represents exceptional success, often the best possible non-critical performance and can determine impales or superior opposed outcomes.

success_bands.label: Critical
success_bands.semantics: An outstanding result, typically represented by a roll of 01. It is better than an extreme success and may produce especially decisive effects such as maximum added damage on an impale.

success_bands.label: Fumble
success_bands.semantics: A catastrophic failure. It cannot be negated by spending Luck and invites severe negative consequences as appropriate to the action, especially in dangerous situations.

play_loop.gm_procedures: Keeper-facing play appears centered on managing investigation flow, clue delivery, pressure, and tone rather than encounter balance. From chapter 10 search hits, the Keeper is expected to adjudicate clue discovery and keep events moving even when players miss or misread evidence (p. 210-212), manage split scenes clearly (p. 211), and aim scenes toward consequences and mounting horror rather than 'winning' combats. Scene framing should therefore start at the next meaningful point of inquiry, danger, or revelation; if the investigators split up, the Keeper should be explicit about whose scene is active and cut between them at tense moments. Rolls are for uncertain, consequential actions; the snippets suggest the Keeper should especially consider how clue access works and avoid stalls around failed interpretation (p. 212). Minimal one-session prep: create a mystery with core clues, decide what the Mythos/human threat is doing if unopposed, prepare a small cast of witnesses/suspects, and line up a few scenes/locations where horror can escalate. Tone prep should emphasize cosmic dread, corruption, and helplessness over fair fights.
play_loop.subsystem_map:
Investigation/clue-gathering/social inquiry: central. This is the apparent default mode of play and the Keeper guidance in chapter 10 seems heavily focused on handling clues, scenes, and pacing.
Sanity/mental deterioration: central. Sanity is a defining pressure track and a major source of consequences for contact with the Mythos (chapter 8; also echoed at p. 166 and p. 184).
Combat: one_of_several. Present and important when violence erupts, but not the game’s main center of gravity.
Chases: one_of_several. A featured procedural mode with dedicated setup and movement rules, used when pursuit matters.
Magic/spell use: minor. Significant fictionally, but dangerous, specialized, and not everyday play; tied to Mythos contact.
Tomes/eldritch research: one_of_several. Important as a gateway to Mythos knowledge, spells, and Sanity risk; supports the investigation loop.
Character creation/skills/general resolution: one_of_several. Core support systems underpin all play but are not the thematic heart compared with investigation plus Sanity.

check_model.summary: Core resolution is percentile roll-under. When the Keeper calls for a roll, the player rolls 1d100 against the relevant skill or other rating. A result above the rating fails; a result equal to or below it succeeds. Difficulty can tighten the target by using a fraction of the rating rather than the full value: the pages read explicitly show a Hard success as rolling less than half the investigator’s Drive Auto skill. Sanity uses the same procedure: the Keeper calls for a Sanity roll, and on failure the investigator loses the listed amount for that encounter (example given: 0/1d6).
check_model.compare_to: the relevant skill or characteristic value; harder difficulties use fractions of that value
check_model.success_rule: Roll 1d100 and succeed if the result is equal to or less than the relevant rating; if a harder difficulty is called for, succeed only if the roll is equal to or less than the required fraction of that rating (explicitly, half for Hard).

game_identity.summary: Lovecraftian investigative horror run by a Keeper. The player characters are investigators who uncover clues, confront human and Mythos threats, and are typically pressured more by fear, uncertainty, and Sanity loss than by tactical victory. The game’s world identity is strongly rooted in H. P. Lovecraft’s cosmic horror: forbidden knowledge, fragile human understanding, and dangerous contact with the Cthulhu Mythos.

procedure.note: The mind is too unhinged to process more horror during the episode.

mechanics_catalog.name: Break down a barrier in a chase

procedure.note: This is resolved as direct damage to the obstacle.

procedure.note: For vehicles, assume high speed.

procedure.note: This is the cost of the attempt.

mechanics_catalog.name: Cast a spell and pay its costs

procedure.note: Most spells require Magic point expenditure to activate.
procedure.condition: Pay the spell’s listed Magic point cost.

procedure.note: This manifests as physical harm chosen by the Keeper.
procedure.condition: If the caster lacks enough Magic points, deduct the excess directly from hit points.

procedure.note: The book states that casting Mythos spells does cost Sanity, though the exact amount is spell-specific.
procedure.condition: Apply any additional spell-specific costs, including Sanity loss where the spell calls for it.

mechanics_catalog.description: Casting a Mythos spell consumes Magic points and may inflict further costs defined by the spell; if the caster has no Magic points left, the excess cost is paid in hit points.
mechanics_catalog.when_to_use: Use whenever an investigator or NPC activates a Mythos spell.

mechanics_catalog.name: Negotiate a chase hazard

procedure.note: Examples include Climb, Swim, Dodge, STR, DEX, or Drive Auto.
procedure.condition: The Keeper names an appropriate skill or characteristic, or accepts a plausible alternative from the player.

procedure.vs: the chosen skill or characteristic at the difficulty set by the Keeper
procedure.note: Resolve the attempt to get through the hazard.
Hazards typically slow characters and can also injure them if mishandled.
procedure.condition: Apply movement loss, delay, harm, or successful movement according to the hazard and result.

mechanics_catalog.description: Each chase location can present a hazard that participants must negotiate with an appropriate skill or characteristic, often at a Keeper-set difficulty.
mechanics_catalog.when_to_use: Use when a fleeing or pursuing character enters a hazardous chase location such as mud, a crowd, a wall, or rough driving terrain.

mechanics_catalog.name: Combat round sequence

procedure.note: Description comes before game terms.
procedure.condition: At the start of combat, ask each player what their investigator is doing in the fiction.

procedure.vs: DEX for initiative under the optional initiative system, or use the default ordering for combatants as applicable
procedure.note: Determine who acts first when needed.
Repeat until all capable participants have acted; then begin a new round.
procedure.condition: On each turn, determine required rolls from the declared action, resolve them, then feed the outcome back into the fiction.

mechanics_catalog.description: Combat is resolved in rounds so every participant gets a chance to act, with actions described in the fiction and then resolved.
mechanics_catalog.when_to_use: Use whenever the situation becomes violent and order of action matters.

mechanics_catalog.name: Combined skill roll

procedure.note: Only one percentile roll is made.
procedure.condition: Name the relevant skills and decide whether success must be achieved on all of them or on only one.

procedure.note: Compare the same result against every listed skill.
Some cases require passing both skills; others allow either skill to succeed.
procedure.condition: Apply the success condition the Keeper declared before the roll.

mechanics_catalog.description: A single percentile roll judged against multiple listed skills, either requiring success on all named skills or on any one of them, as the Keeper specifies.
mechanics_catalog.when_to_use: Use when a task meaningfully depends on more than one capability at once, or when different aptitudes could each allow the investigator to react effectively to the same situation.

The investigator did not learn from that use.

procedure.note: Add 1D10 to the skill immediately.

procedure.note: If these conditions are met, the character can flee melee on their turn.

Describe the escape.

procedure.note: Use Dodge if evading; use an appropriate Fighting skill if countering.
procedure.condition: The defender chooses either to dodge or to fight back.

procedure.note: Make the attack roll.
Resolve the chosen response.
If the attacker beats a dodging defender, damage is dealt; if the dodger ties or wins, no damage. If fighting back, the higher success wins the exchange.
procedure.condition: Compare success levels.

procedure.note: The spell names should usually be presented in-fiction rather than by rulebook title.
procedure.condition: The Keeper also reveals and summarizes any spells present in the book.

procedure.note: This inflicts a major wound.

Use the dying procedure.

procedure.condition: If the pushed roll fails, apply a serious consequence appropriate to the method and situation.

mechanics_catalog.description: A player may turn a failed non-combat skill attempt into a riskier renewed effort, with higher stakes if it fails.
mechanics_catalog.when_to_use: Use after a failed skill roll when the investigator could plausibly try again with more effort, more time, or greater risk, and the Keeper is willing to define a meaningful consequence for failure.

mechanics_catalog.name: Resolve a ranged or thrown attack

procedure.note: Thrown and missile attacks use firearm-style difficulty setting.
procedure.condition: Set the attack's difficulty from range and circumstances.

procedure.note: Missile attacks may be answered with Dive for Cover; thrown weapons may be opposed with Dodge like a fighting attack. A character cannot fight back against a ranged or thrown attack unless within one-fifth of their DEX in feet of the attacker.
procedure.condition: Determine the defender's options.

procedure.vs: the relevant ranged attack skill at the set difficulty
procedure.note: Resolve the hit roll after applying any situational modifiers.

A readied firearm gains the +50 DEX benefit only before any movement; moving up to MOV allows a normal firearms attack on usual DEX rank; moving up to MOV×5 means firing while running and losing that advantage.
procedure.condition: If moving with a firearm, apply the movement limits for when the shot occurs.

mechanics_catalog.description: Procedure for attacks made with firearms, bows, or thrown weapons, including which defensive options apply and how movement and cover interact with the shot.
mechanics_catalog.when_to_use: Use when a combatant attacks from range with a firearm, missile weapon, or thrown object.

mechanics_catalog.name: Reality check during underlying insanity

procedure.note: Make a reality check.
They resist further delusions until they lose more Sanity.
procedure.condition: On success, the investigator sees through the delusion and the Keeper must describe reality accurately.

procedure.note: If the investigator is suffering underlying insanity, this immediately induces a bout of madness.
procedure.condition: On failure, lose 1 Sanity point.

mechanics_catalog.description: An investigator suffering underlying insanity may challenge a possible delusion with a Sanity roll to determine what is really there.
mechanics_catalog.when_to_use: Use when an investigator under underlying insanity doubts what they are perceiving and asks whether an apparent sight or event is real.
mechanics_catalog.locked_until: Only available while the investigator is suffering underlying insanity and is confronting a possible delusion.

mechanics_catalog.name: Sanity roll and Sanity loss

procedure.note: Make a Sanity roll.
The exact amount depends on the encounter.
procedure.condition: On success, apply the lower listed Sanity loss if any.

procedure.note: The player or Keeper rolls the listed loss amount when needed.
procedure.condition: On failure, apply the higher listed Sanity loss.

mechanics_catalog.description: Exposure to horrific truths, monsters, or Mythos events can call for a Sanity roll, with success or failure determining how much Sanity is lost.
mechanics_catalog.when_to_use: Use when an investigator encounters something the rules or scenario deem sanity-blasting, such as a monster, revelation, or supernatural event.

mechanics_catalog.name: Self-help Sanity recovery

procedure.note: Examples include a retreat, holiday, or reconnecting with a loved one.
procedure.condition: Roleplay or describe what the investigator is doing to recover, tied to their backstory or key connection.

procedure.note: Make a Sanity roll; use a bonus die if the investigator is using their key connection.
If the key connection was used, the investigator also recovers from indefinite insanity.
procedure.condition: On success, recover 1D6 Sanity points.

procedure.note: If the failed aspect was the key connection, it is lost.
procedure.condition: On failure, lose 1 Sanity point and revise that backstory aspect to reflect the failed attempt.

mechanics_catalog.description: During downtime or development, an investigator may seek healing through meaningful backstory connections or personal restoration scenes.
mechanics_catalog.when_to_use: Use between adventures or during the investigator development phase when the player describes a thematically appropriate attempt at healing or redemption.

mechanics_catalog.name: Spend Luck after a roll

procedure.note: Luck cannot alter another character’s roll.
procedure.condition: The roll must be the investigator’s own skill or characteristic roll.

procedure.note: Criticals, fumbles, and firearm malfunctions still stand.
procedure.condition: The roll must not be a Luck roll, damage roll, Sanity roll, Sanity-loss amount roll, or a pushed roll.

procedure.note: Deduct Luck equal to the amount by which the rolled value must be lowered.
procedure.amount: as many points as needed on a 1-for-1 basis

procedure.note: No skill improvement check is earned if Luck changed the roll.
procedure.condition: Change the roll result accordingly and resolve the new outcome band.

mechanics_catalog.description: Luck points can be spent on a 1-for-1 basis to improve the result of the investigator’s own skill or characteristic roll after seeing the dice.
mechanics_catalog.when_to_use: Use immediately after the investigator makes a skill or characteristic roll and before the fiction moves on, when a better success band would matter and the roll is eligible for Luck spending.
mechanics_catalog.locked_until: Only available if the table is using the optional Luck-spending rule.

mechanics_catalog.name: Temporary insanity trigger

procedure.note: This is the trigger threshold.
procedure.condition: The investigator has lost 5 or more Sanity points at one time.

procedure.note: Roll to see whether the investigator fully comprehends what was experienced.
Proceed to a bout of madness.
procedure.condition: If the INT roll succeeds, temporary insanity begins immediately and lasts 1D10 hours.

procedure.note: The Sanity loss still stands.
procedure.condition: If the INT roll fails, the memory is repressed and the investigator does not become insane from this trigger.

mechanics_catalog.description: A large immediate Sanity loss can force the investigator to grasp the full significance of the horror and thereby become temporarily insane.
mechanics_catalog.when_to_use: Use when an investigator loses 5 or more Sanity points from a single shock.

mechanics_catalog.name: Zero hit points and dying

procedure.note: Do not track negative hit points.
This always happens at zero hit points.
procedure.condition: The character is unconscious.

procedure.note: No dying procedure begins.
procedure.condition: If the character only took regular damage, they do not die and will heal in time.

procedure.note: They require successful First Aid for temporary stabilization, then Medicine or hospitalization.
procedure.condition: If the character is at 0 hit points while suffering a major wound, they are dying.

mechanics_catalog.description: At 0 HP an investigator is unconscious. If a major wound is also in effect, the character is dying and needs immediate stabilization.
mechanics_catalog.when_to_use: Use as soon as current hit points are reduced to 0 or below.
mechanics_catalog.passive_projection: HP {value}: unconscious at 0; dying if also under Major Wound

character_sheet_schema.title: Call Of Cthulhu Keeper Rulebook 40th Anniversary (Sandy Petersen) Character Template

fields.notes: The investigator’s profession. It informs what they plausibly know and do in play, and helps frame roleplay and scenario access.
fields.title: Occupation

fields.notes: Age matters in the fiction and can affect how the investigator is portrayed at the table.
fields.title: Age

fields.notes: A descriptive identity field used for portrayal in play.
fields.title: Sex

fields.notes: Where the investigator lives; useful for framing scenes, contacts, and personal stakes.
fields.title: Residence

fields.notes: The investigator’s place of origin; used for background and characterization.
fields.title: Birthplace

fields.notes: Strength. Used when brute force or physical power is tested, and to judge physical limits.
fields.title: STR

fields.notes: Constitution. Used to resist collapse, remain conscious after major trauma, endure dying, and in speed rolls for chases.
fields.title: CON

fields.notes: Size. Used when bulk or mass matters and in some opposed physical situations.
fields.title: SIZ

fields.notes: Dexterity. Used for agility, reaction, initiative, and some chase hazards.
fields.title: DEX

fields.notes: Appearance. A social characteristic that may matter when first impressions or presence are tested.
fields.title: APP

fields.notes: Intelligence. Used for recognizing the full significance of a Sanity-shaking revelation and thus whether temporary insanity begins.
fields.title: INT

fields.notes: Power. The source characteristic for Magic points; also central to magical resilience and will.
fields.title: POW

fields.notes: Education. Represents formal learning and is relevant to scholarship and comprehension.
fields.title: EDU

fields.notes: Current Sanity points. This track falls from trauma and Mythos exposure, can trigger insanity, and can recover through treatment or self-help. It cannot exceed maximum Sanity.
fields.title: SAN

fields.notes: Current physical health. At 0 HP the investigator is unconscious; major wounds and dying depend on HP loss.
fields.title: Hit Points

fields.notes: Current magical energy. Spells usually spend Magic points first; if they run out, further magical cost comes from hit points.
fields.title: Magic Points

fields.notes: A spendable pool that may be used after a skill or characteristic roll to improve the result on a 1-for-1 basis, subject to restrictions. It may recover between sessions.
fields.title: Luck

fields.notes: The investigator’s movement value. It is central to chases and may be temporarily adjusted by speed rolls.
fields.title: Move Rate

fields.notes: Extra melee damage based on build/strength. It is added to relevant weapon or unarmed damage, including impales.
fields.title: Damage Bonus

fields.notes: A measure of physical mass and force. It affects melee damage and determines how much damage a vehicle inflicts when smashing a barrier in a chase.
fields.title: Build

fields.notes: Printed on standard investigator sheet.
fields.title: Armor

fields.notes: Ready money available for immediate spending in play.
fields.title: Cash

fields.notes: Property and wealth holdings that reflect the investigator’s broader means and social-economic position.
fields.title: Assets

fields.notes: The level of everyday purchases the investigator can make without special concern.
fields.title: Spending Level

fields.notes: A record of skill points granted by occupation; mainly relevant as background for the sheet.
fields.title: Occupation Skill Points

fields.notes: A record of non-occupation skill points; mainly relevant as background for the sheet.
fields.title: Personal Interest Skill Points

fields.notes: Also functions as resource/status measure.
fields.title: Credit Rating

fields.notes: The sheet’s handgun combat skill, used when attacking with pistols and similar weapons.
fields.title: Firearms (Handgun)

fields.notes: The sheet’s rifle/shotgun combat skill, used for rifles and shotguns and some single-shot long arms.
fields.title: Firearms (Rifle/Shotgun)

fields.notes: The basic melee combat skill, used for fistfights and improvised simple hand weapons.
fields.title: Fighting (Brawl)

fields.notes: Used to evade attacks in combat and to avoid some chase hazards.
fields.title: Dodge

fields.notes: The investigator’s native language skill, relevant for comprehension and communication.
fields.title: Language (Own)

fields.notes: The sheet records the full skill list from Chapter 4, including specialty lines and custom entries.
fields.title: Occupation/Personal Interest Skill Entries

fields.notes: Important carried or owned items. These can be lost, stolen, damaged, or altered during play.
fields.title: Possessions

fields.notes: The collection of personal background entries that ground roleplay and can be altered by insanity.
fields.title: Backstory

fields.notes: A short portrayal of the investigator’s look and manner for roleplay reference.
fields.title: Description

fields.notes: A record of lasting physical harm; major injuries may add or change entries here over time.
fields.title: Injuries & Scars

fields.notes: People important to the investigator; they can become anchors for recovery or be transformed by madness.
fields.title: Significant People

fields.notes: Places emotionally important to the investigator; these can be used in roleplay and recovery.
fields.title: Meaningful Locations

fields.notes: Items of special personal importance; insanity or robbery may threaten them.
fields.title: Treasured Possessions

fields.notes: Key personality traits for roleplay; insanity may alter them.
fields.title: Traits

fields.notes: Core beliefs and convictions; bouts of madness may distort or replace them.
fields.title: Ideology/Beliefs

fields.notes: A standing record of mental conditions gained through play, especially insanity.
fields.title: Phobias & Manias

fields.notes: A history field recording exposure to the uncanny and Mythos, useful for continuity and roleplay.
fields.title: Encounters with Strange Entities

fields.notes: Use the Chapter 4 skill list as the schema for all printed skill rows.
fields.title: Full Skill Table

creation_flow.title: Choose age and apply age adjustments

validation_rules.description: Credit Rating must be set within the range listed by the chosen occupation.
Occupation skill allocations must total exactly the occupation’s listed skill point formula result.
Personal interest skill allocations must total INT × 2.
Personal interest points may not be spent on Cthulhu Mythos during initial investigator creation.
When a skill requires a specialty, the specialty must be named and tracked separately (for example Art/Craft, Science, Language Other, Fighting, Firearms).
Hard and Extreme values use the quick-reference half and fifth values from p61, effectively rounding down fractions.
If age is selected, all required age-based adjustments and EDU improvement checks must be applied.

play_loop.gm_procedures: Keeper-facing play appears centered on managing investigation flow, clue delivery, pressure, and tone rather than encounter balance. From chapter 10 search hits, the Keeper is expected to adjudicate clue discovery and keep events moving even when players miss or misread evidence (p. 210-212), manage split scenes clearly (p. 211), and aim scenes toward consequences and mounting horror rather than 'winning' combats. Scene framing should therefore start at the next meaningful point of inquiry, danger, or revelation; if the investigators split up, the Keeper should be explicit about whose scene is active and cut between them at tense moments. Rolls are for uncertain, consequential actions; the snippets suggest the Keeper should especially consider how clue access works and avoid stalls around failed interpretation (p. 212). Minimal one-session prep: create a mystery with core clues, decide what the Mythos/human threat is doing if unopposed, prepare a small cast of witnesses/suspects, and line up a few scenes/locations where horror can escalate. Tone prep should emphasize cosmic dread, corruption, and helplessness over fair fights.
play_loop.subsystem_map:
Investigation/clue-gathering/social inquiry: central. This is the apparent default mode of play and the Keeper guidance in chapter 10 seems heavily focused on handling clues, scenes, and pacing.
Sanity/mental deterioration: central. Sanity is a defining pressure track and a major source of consequences for contact with the Mythos (chapter 8; also echoed at p. 166 and p. 184).
Combat: one_of_several. Present and important when violence erupts, but not the game’s main center of gravity.
Chases: one_of_several. A featured procedural mode with dedicated setup and movement rules, used when pursuit matters.
Magic/spell use: minor. Significant fictionally, but dangerous, specialized, and not everyday play; tied to Mythos contact.
Tomes/eldritch research: one_of_several. Important as a gateway to Mythos knowledge, spells, and Sanity risk; supports the investigation loop.
Character creation/skills/general resolution: one_of_several. Core support systems underpin all play but are not the thematic heart compared with investigation plus Sanity.

game_identity.summary: Lovecraftian investigative horror run by a Keeper. The player characters are investigators who uncover clues, confront human and Mythos threats, and are typically pressured more by fear, uncertainty, and Sanity loss than by tactical victory. The game’s world identity is strongly rooted in H. P. Lovecraft’s cosmic horror: forbidden knowledge, fragile human understanding, and dangerous contact with the Cthulhu Mythos.

value.title: Triangle 6d4 Conflict Resolution
value.summary: Roll six four-sided dice and interpret results according to Triangle Agency's conflict and performance rules.

play_loop.gm_procedures: Keeper-facing play appears centered on managing investigation flow, clue delivery, pressure, and tone rather than encounter balance. From chapter 10 search hits, the Keeper is expected to adjudicate clue discovery and keep events moving even when players miss or misread evidence (p. 210-212), manage split scenes clearly (p. 211), and aim scenes toward consequences and mounting horror rather than 'winning' combats. Scene framing should therefore start at the next meaningful point of inquiry, danger, or revelation; if the investigators split up, the Keeper should be explicit about whose scene is active and cut between them at tense moments. Rolls are for uncertain, consequential actions; the snippets suggest the Keeper should especially consider how clue access works and avoid stalls around failed interpretation (p. 212). Minimal one-session prep: create a mystery with core clues, decide what the Mythos/human threat is doing if unopposed, prepare a small cast of witnesses/suspects, and line up a few scenes/locations where horror can escalate. Tone prep should emphasize cosmic dread, corruption, and helplessness over fair fights.
play_loop.subsystem_map:
Investigation/clue-gathering/social inquiry: central. This is the apparent default mode of play and the Keeper guidance in chapter 10 seems heavily focused on handling clues, scenes, and pacing.
Sanity/mental deterioration: central. Sanity is a defining pressure track and a major source of consequences for contact with the Mythos (chapter 8; also echoed at p. 166 and p. 184).
Combat: one_of_several. Present and important when violence erupts, but not the game’s main center of gravity.
Chases: one_of_several. A featured procedural mode with dedicated setup and movement rules, used when pursuit matters.
Magic/spell use: minor. Significant fictionally, but dangerous, specialized, and not everyday play; tied to Mythos contact.
Tomes/eldritch research: one_of_several. Important as a gateway to Mythos knowledge, spells, and Sanity risk; supports the investigation loop.
Character creation/skills/general resolution: one_of_several. Core support systems underpin all play but are not the thematic heart compared with investigation plus Sanity.

game_identity.summary: Lovecraftian investigative horror run by a Keeper. The player characters are investigators who uncover clues, confront human and Mythos threats, and are typically pressured more by fear, uncertainty, and Sanity loss than by tactical victory. The game’s world identity is strongly rooted in H. P. Lovecraft’s cosmic horror: forbidden knowledge, fragile human understanding, and dangerous contact with the Cthulhu Mythos.

I was one of those annoying precocious kids who read a lot,

interesting to check out. This is where I encountered both
Edgar Rice Burroughs and Edgar Allan Poe, among others.

material_index.title: Charm (15%)
material_index.summary:
Charm takes many forms, including physical attraction,
seduction, flattery or simply warmth of personality. Charm
may be used to compel someone to act in a certain way, but
not in a manner completely contrary to that person’s normal
behavior. Charm is opposed by the Charm or Psychology skills.
Charm may be used for bargaining, to haggle the price of
an item or service down. If successful, the seller is won over
and they may well reduce the price a little.

material_index.summary:
This skill allows a character to climb trees, walls and other
vertical surfaces with or without ropes and climbing gear.
The skill also encompasses rappelling.
Conditions such as firmness of surface, available handholds,
wind, visibility, rain, etc., may all affect the difficulty level.
Failing this skill on the first roll indicates that the climb
is perhaps beyond the investigator’s capability. Failing a
pushed roll is likely to indicate a fall with resultant damage.

material_index.title: Pushed Roll: Success

The player’s goal is achieved as it would have been for the

material_index.title: Pushed Roll: Failure
material_index.summary:
Failing a pushed roll grants the Keeper free rein over the
     outcome, including damage, Sanity checks, loss of equipment,
     isolation from the rest of the investigators, capture, and so
     on. The Keeper can even incorporate the player’s goal being
     achieved (even though the player failed the pushed roll), but
     at some form of cost.
         When a player fails a pushed roll, he or she is giving the
     Keeper license to make the investigators’ lives more difficult.

material_index.summary:
If a player describes a goal other than simply inflicting
physical harm, such as disarming their opponent or knocking
them over, then it can be resolved with a maneuver. This
may include pushing someone out of the way, throwing the
opponent to the floor, restraining someone in a headlock,
disarming an opponent, and so on.

material_index.title: Regular Damage: The Effects
material_index.summary:
Regular damage is the result of any single attack that deals
damage equal to less than half the character’s maximum hit
points in a single blow. It has no significant effect on the
character until current hit points are reduced to zero, when
the character will become unconscious. A character cannot
die as a result of regular damage.

material_index.title: Unconsciousness and Death
material_index.summary:
Call of Cthulhu is a horror game and sometimes it may be
more terrifying for an investigator to stay conscious; if the
Keeper wishes, a character may be incapacitated rather than
fully unconscious. Equally, final death does not have to occur
instantaneously, and the light in a character’s eyes might not
go out until after a particularly dramatic moment or once their
final words have been uttered (at the Keeper’s discretion).

Parts 1 to 4 have covered all of the essential chase rules.

material_index.title: Choosing a Route
material_index.summary:
It is the nature of a chase that the character being chased (the
quarry) wants nothing other than to escape and must make
split-second decisions whether to turn left or right. If there
is a choice of routes available, the lead character is free to
choose and may seek a more difficult path or an easier one,
especially if he or she feels it would be to their advantage to
do so. For example, a strong swimmer might opt to leap into
the river to lose their pursuer. If the investigator is the one

material_index.summary:

the players by describing new terrain that constantly works
against the investigators. You may find it more fun all round
to create hazards and barriers randomly.

mean that it will remain that way. A car may suddenly pull

someone might come running around the corner from
the opposite direction, a loose dog might assault a fleeing
investigator, and so on.

investigator’s path. Once an investigator has lost as many

material_index.title: Insane Insight
material_index.summary:
When an investigator goes insane (either temporarily or

indefinitely), he or she has a momentary insane insight.

This moment of clarity provides a clue or action that might

benefit the investigator(s) immediately or at some later

stage. The Keeper should determine an appropriate insight

relevant to the plot of the scenario.

high tension, over-the-top schlock horror, or a pulp-action romp
Having said that, the default mode for this game is intended to
horror with some action scenes thrown into the mix.

You should decide, as a group, whether the game is to be

serious or jocular. Comedy and horror are good bedfellows

and the switch from one to the other is used to great effect in

many movies. However, too much comedy lessens the horror.

ordinary and acceptable then. Racism, xenophobia, religious

bias, and sexual discrimination were part of everyday life and

material_index.summary:
Expect the players to investigate and ask questions. That
statement may sound obvious; however, these investigations

will lead the players to ask questions regarding matters you
have not considered. If there has been a murder, for example,
you need to have a clear vision of what has occurred at
the scene. You also need to decide how the murder took
place. A player may ask if there are muddy footprints on
the study carpet, whether there are any witnesses, or if the

material_index.title: Perception Rolls
material_index.summary:
There are three main perception skills in Call of Cthulhu:

i Spot Hidden: Chiefly visual observation, though it
can also be used for smell or taste.

i Listen: Perceiving and identifying sounds.
i Psychology: Understanding the motivations and
intentions of another person.

If a player succeeds in a roll for a perception skill, some
information pertinent to the scenario should be forthcoming
(referred to as a clue).

material_index.summary:

characteristics and creating an investigator. A variety of
alternative approaches are presented in Chapter 3: Creating

material_index.title: Winners and Losers
material_index.summary:
Call of Cthulhu is not a competition between you and the

players. The rules ensure that everyone is treated fairly;

however, there is no mechanism to enforce game balance
between the Keeper and the players. Balance is derived from
the decisions that you make as Keeper. You decide what the
investigators encounter, you set the scene, you decide on the
actions of the non-player characters.

material_index.title: Fair Warning
material_index.summary:
Keepers should endeavor to provide players with the chance
to avoid investigator death wherever possible. This is not to
say that Keepers should diminish the abilities of monsters
and villains in the game, or pull their punches when dealing
out damage from attacks and other injuries. Rather, it is
recommended that Keepers give players up to three chances
to avoid certain death.

material_index.title: Failed Sanity Rolls
material_index.summary:
A sense of self-control is an essential quality of sanity. A non-
player character may hold a gun to an investigator’s head and
demand information regarding a missing segment of the
R’lyeh Disk, but whether the investigator tells or accepts a
bullet in the head is up to the player. However, when a Sanity
roll is failed, the investigator loses all self-control and may
act in a way that is counter to his or her best interests.
People who lose control may harm themselves or others,
even loved ones,

material_index.title: to Listed Spells
material_index.summary:
A spell is made up of three parts: a cost, a description, and

an effect. Cost and effect have a direct mechanical impact on

the game that may include sanity loss, physical damage, loss

of magic points, permanent change to characteristics, and

so forth. You are free to alter these things, although some
careful consideration is required; placing a cheap, powerful
spell into the hands of the players can have a dramatic

effect upon play. Description, on the other hand, is simply

dramatic color

material_index.title: Opposed POW Rolls
material_index.summary:
Many spells call for a POW roll to be made to test whether

the spell affects its target. Both sides make a POW roll and

compare their levels of success, with the higher one being

the victor. In the case of a tie, the higher POW wins; if the

sides are still drawn, the Keeper might decide that both

are affected adversely in some manner that reflects the

nature of the spell. If the difference between the caster’s

POW and the target’s POW is 100 or more, the one with

the greater POW automati

material_index.title: Spell Range
material_index.summary:
In the game, spell range is usually one of three options:

touch, 100 yards, or sight with the unaided eye. These

general choices are easy to visualize and understand.

Greater ranges can become engineering problems, not

examples of horror.

material_index.title: Casting Time
material_index.summary:
and Spells in Combat

Some spells are useful in combat situations. Each spell has

a casting time listed in its description: instantaneous, 1

round, and so on.

If the casting time is instantaneous, it activates on the

user’s DEX+50 (just like a readied gun).

If the casting takes one round, it activates on the user’s

DEX in the present round.

If the casting takes two rounds, it activates on the

user’s DEX in the following round, and so on.

material_index.summary:
Try to insert some personal touches to the spell, tying it

more strongly to your scenario, investigators, and story,

if possible.

Location: consider the locations in your story; could
one of them be linked to the spell? If the investigators are
dealing with ghouls, for example, a spell that must be cast

underground suddenly takes on an added dimension.

Spell components: the specific items required to

cast the spell. Could it be that the investigators need the

more complex and involved ritual. Consider where,

when, and how the spell is cast. Do the investigators

inscribe a ritual circle?

dramatic. Try to imbue the description with strange smells,

sensations—remember that most of these spells erode

material_index.title: One Spell with Variations
material_index.summary:
A spell could be compared with a cooking recipe. There
is no definitive bread recipe; soda bread can be made in
an hour while sourdough bread takes days. A variety of

flours and other ingredients may be used. The methods

of making can vary; it can be done by hand or with a

machine. The resulting breads come in all shapes, sizes,

and flavors. If you look at ten cookbooks, you will find

many differing recipes for bread with many different

names. The same is true for spells and tomes.

between the player characters and their enemies. Nor is
there a level-based structure into which spells must fit.

useful to understand the differences.

Call spells are immensely powerful rituals that bring

an actual physical manifestation of a god before the caster.

Call spells may be used by cults to bring forth their dark

gods to accept ritual sacrifices or as an act of worship.

The flip-side of the Call spell is the Dismiss spell, used to

send the god back from whence it came. Dismiss spells

may well prove useful to the investigators.

section_path: chapter 14: monsters , beasts , and alien gods

material_index.title: —Ramsey Campbell, Cold Print
material_index.summary:
Y’golonac is delineated in the Revelations of Gla'aki, an arcane
book. It is a bloated, glowing figure who dwells underground
in a vast ruin behind a wall of bricks. This prison may be
near the Severn Valley city of Brichester, for it is known to
frequent that place. Y’golonac is known to come when its
name is read or spoken while evil is present. It is a minor
god, but malignant.

section_path: chapter 14: monsters , beasts , and alien gods

material_index.title: Cult
material_index.summary:
Y’golonac has little cult following, but strives mightily after
more worship, entrapping those who are subtly evil to be his
priests. Y’Golonac’s notion of evil seems to be a shallow one,
however.

section_path: chapter 14: monsters , beasts , and alien gods

Old Ones or Outer Gods—byakhee with Hastur, for instance,
or nightgaunts with Nodens. These are servitor species,
and frequently an Outer God or Great Old One manifests
accompanied by several such servitors. Representatives
may act as assassins, messengers, spies, and delivery boys,
frightening off investigators and bulking out confrontations.
In comparison, Outer Gods and Great Old Ones should be

try to barter for more pay or to get another investigator’s
share. There’s also the option of the ransom that Harris ran
off with. Strong wants it back, but the desperate investigator
could always try to snatch it.

wanted to save a few bucks. He did nothing wrong and it’s

their way back and forth from the hole to the furthest hut

attach to the crystal to pull it to the surface. At night they ar

material_index.summary:
Your sleep is far from restful. You toss and turn from
side to side, bombarded throughout the hours of
darkness by images that you barely recall when you
awake. Maybe it’s the previous day’s trek through the
forest that’s influencing this. All you remember are the
dark trees surrounding you, the sickly, yellowing leaves
falling to the ground. You feel a terrible foreboding.
Something is out there. Watching. Waiting…

material_index.summary:
Yellow leaves fall slowly from the thick roof of

branches above. Blades of sunlight stab through the

darkness. Ahead of you stands a dilapidated log cabin.

They advance slowly with purpose. You want to turn

material_index.title: Conclusion
material_index.summary:
Call of Cthulhu was created over 30 years ago by Sandy
Petersen. There have been very few changes in those 30 years.
The aim of this new edition is to retain the aspects that made
Call of Cthulhu so much fun to play and at the same time
introduce some new rules that provide the Keeper and players
with additional ways to create drama and excitement, such as
the ability to push rolls and run chase scenes.
We hope that you enjoy this new edition.

material_index.title: Sanity Rules
material_index.summary:
Failing a Sanity roll: one involuntary action.

Sanity loss of 5 points or more: make an Intelligence roll—if
successful, temporary insanity ensues.

Sanity loss of one-fifth or more in one day: indefinite
insanity ensues.

material_index.title: The Phases of Insanity
material_index.summary:
A bout of madness: either "real time" (1D10 rounds) or
"summary" (1D10 hours); Keeper amends one backstory
detail (phobia, mania, etc.)
Underlying Insanity: any further Sanity loss results in
another bout of madness; the investigator is prone to
delusions.

material_index.title: The Side-Effects of Insanity
material_index.summary:
1. Phobias: while insane, must fight/flee or take a penalty di
on skill rolls.
2. Manias: while insane, must submit to mania or take a
penalty die on skill rolls.
3. Delusions and Reality Checks: make a Sanity roll to test
for delusions:
Failure: lose 1 Sanity point (and undergo a bout of
madness if insane).
Success: dismiss delusions.
4. Insanity and the Cthulhu Mythos: add 5% Cthulhu
Mythos skill with first bout of madness inspired by a Mythos-
related event. Add 1% on subsequent occasions.

material_index.title: Recovery
material_index.summary:
From temporary insanity: after 1D10 hours or a good rest.

From indefinite insanity: roll at the end of each month of
treatment; Keeper may allow automatic recovery during the
next investigator development phase.

Treatment with private/home care (roll 1D100 per month):
01–95: success (or under psychoanalysis skill); add 1D3
Sanity points. Make a Sanity roll—if successful, insanity is
cured.

The body of Walter Corbitt is buried in the basement of the
Corbitt house. The mind of Walter Corbitt still lives, aware of
events within the house. He haunts the place. Corbitt knows
Mythos magic that preserves his identity and enables him
to animate his body after death. He sometimes vampirically
preys upon residents of the house, driving away or slaying
those who learn his secret.

material_index.title: About W. Corbitt, Esq
material_index.summary:
He might be silent at first, but at some point during
the confrontation with the investigators it will be more
convincing to have him growl, screech, cackle, or mock. He
does not breathe at all.
Corbitt is not truly a vampire, nor any recognizable monster—
he is a sorcerer in the process of transforming himself into
something entirely inhuman.
Sunlight causes him pain and is too bright for him to see
comfortably. It might kill him, but whether it does so is for the

validation_rules.description: Credit Rating must be set within the range listed by the chosen occupation.
Occupation skill allocations must total exactly the occupation’s listed skill point formula result.
Personal interest skill allocations must total INT × 2.
Personal interest points may not be spent on Cthulhu Mythos during initial investigator creation.

Hard and Extreme values use the quick-reference half and fifth values from p61, effectively rounding down fractions.
If age is selected, all required age-based adjustments and EDU improvement checks must be applied.
